---
title: "Babqua x Nushell — Clojure-shaped pipelines in a notebook"
filters:
  - bb
---

This page demonstrates running [Nushell](https://www.nushell.sh) pipelines
from inside Babqua-evaluated `{.clojure .bb}` blocks — using
[`nu_plugin_edn`](https://github.com/franks42/nu_plugin_edn) to flow
typed structured data between Clojure and Nushell over EDN bytes.

Each block starts a fresh `nu` process, pipes EDN to its stdin, and reads
EDN back from its stdout. The result is rendered by Babqua's Kindly
machinery — table, code, chart, whichever the block's metadata declares.

## Setup

Two helpers hide the shell/stdin/stdout plumbing:

```{.clojure .bb}
(require '[babashka.process :as p]
         '[clojure.edn :as edn]
         '[clojure.string :as str])

;; Prepend the demo's bin/ dir to PATH for any subprocess we spawn,
;; so adjacent ^cedn / ^uuidv7 binaries are discoverable without a
;; system-wide install. Path is resolved relative to the file the bb
;; runtime is invoked from — Quarto runs bb from the .qmd's project
;; root, so "bin" resolves correctly here. If you move this notebook,
;; adjust accordingly.
(def ^:private demo-bin
  (-> (java.io.File. "bin") .getAbsolutePath))

(defn- subprocess-env []
  (assoc (into {} (System/getenv))
         "PATH" (str demo-bin java.io.File/pathSeparator
                     (or (System/getenv "PATH") ""))))

(defn nu->
  "Run `pipeline` (a nu command string) with `input` piped to stdin.
   `input` is pr-str'd as EDN if not already a string. Returns the
   raw stdout string. Uses `nu --stdin -c` so the pipeline's first
   command receives the bb-side stdin. The demo's bin/ dir is
   prepended to PATH so nu can find ^cedn / ^uuidv7 without a system
   install.

   Throws on non-zero exit, surfacing stderr in the exception
   message — so failures (missing external CLI, plugin not loaded,
   pipeline syntax error) become a visible error block in the
   notebook instead of silently producing empty output."
  [input pipeline]
  (let [stdin (cond
                (string? input) input
                (nil? input)    ""
                :else           (pr-str input))
        {:keys [out err exit]} (p/sh {:in stdin :extra-env {"PATH" (get (subprocess-env) "PATH")}}
                                     "nu" "--stdin" "-c" pipeline)]
    (when-not (zero? exit)
      (throw (ex-info (str "nu pipeline failed (exit " exit "):\n"
                           (str/trim err)
                           "\n  pipeline: " pipeline)
                      {:exit exit :pipeline pipeline :stderr err :stdout out})))
    out))

(defn nu->edn
  "Like `nu->` but parses stdout as a SINGLE EDN value. The pipeline
   must produce EDN bytes on stdout — typically by ending with
   `to edn`, `^cedn`, `^uuidv7 gen --format edn`, or any other
   EDN-emitting tail command. The contract is the bytes' shape, not
   the tail name; we don't pre-validate the pipeline string.

   Strict parse: reads one EDN value, then checks the rest of stdout
   is whitespace-only. Catches the case where a forgotten `to edn`
   leaves a Nushell table-rendering on stdout (`╭───┬───╮\\n│ ... │`)
   — the table-drawing chars happen to be legal Clojure symbol
   chars, so a naive `edn/read-string` would silently return a bogus
   symbol value. The strict check rejects with a useful error
   instead.

   On any failure, raises with a stdout snippet and a hint pointing
   at the typical fix."
  [input pipeline]
  (let [out (nu-> input pipeline)
        snippet (subs out 0 (min 200 (count out)))
        ellipsis (when (> (count out) 200) "...")
        fail (fn [reason cause]
               (throw (ex-info (str "nu pipeline stdout is not a single EDN value\n"
                                    "  reason:   " reason "\n"
                                    "  pipeline: " pipeline "\n"
                                    "  stdout:   " (pr-str (str snippet ellipsis)) "\n"
                                    "  hint: end the pipeline with `to edn`, `^cedn`,"
                                    " `^uuidv7 gen --format edn`,"
                                    " or another EDN-emitting command")
                               (cond-> {:pipeline pipeline :stdout out}
                                 cause (assoc :cause cause)))))]
    (let [rdr (java.io.PushbackReader. (java.io.StringReader. out))
          eof (Object.)
          v   (try (edn/read {:eof eof} rdr)
                   (catch Throwable t (fail (str "parse error: " (.getMessage t)) t)))]
      (when (= v eof)
        (fail "empty stdout — pipeline produced nothing" nil))
      (let [trailing (slurp rdr)]
        (when-not (str/blank? trailing)
          (fail (str "trailing non-whitespace content after first parsed value:\n  "
                     (pr-str (subs trailing 0 (min 80 (count trailing)))))
                nil)))
      v)))

(defn nu-loaded?
  "Quick sanity check that nu_plugin_edn is registered."
  []
  (= "1\n" (nu-> nil "plugin list | where name == edn | length")))

(defn which
  "Return the path to `cmd` on PATH (with demo's bin/ prepended), or
   nil if not found."
  [cmd]
  (let [{:keys [out exit]} (p/sh {:extra-env {"PATH" (get (subprocess-env) "PATH")}}
                                 "which" cmd)]
    (when (zero? exit) (str/trim out))))
```

### Preflight diagnostic

Before the sections that depend on external CLIs, see what's actually
on PATH. If `^cedn` or `^uuidv7` shows missing here, the corresponding
sections will throw with a clear error rather than render empty data.

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/table
[{:tool "nu"            :path (or (which "nu") "MISSING")     :needed-for "all sections"}
 {:tool "bb"            :path (or (which "bb") "MISSING")     :needed-for "the runtime itself"}
 {:tool "nu_plugin_edn" :path (if (nu-loaded?) "registered" "NOT REGISTERED") :needed-for "all sections"}
 {:tool "^cedn"         :path (or (which "cedn") "MISSING")   :needed-for "sections 2 & 4"}
 {:tool "^uuidv7"       :path (or (which "uuidv7") "MISSING") :needed-for "sections 3 & 4"}]
```

## 1. bb → nu → bb: filter and sort via Nushell

Push some Clojure data through `from edn | where ... | sort-by | to edn`
and read the structured result back. Babqua's `^:kind/table` metadata
renders the returned vector of maps as an HTML table. 

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/table
(nu->edn
  [{:filename "report.pdf" :size 142857}
   {:filename "scratch"    :size 4096}
   {:filename "data.csv"   :size 99999}
   {:filename "tiny.txt"   :size 64}]
  "from edn | where size > 1000 | sort-by size --reverse | to edn")
```

The filter / sort happens inside Nushell. Same data flowing in could be
a 10K-row `bb produce.clj` stream and the pattern would be identical —
incremental over the pipe via `--lines`. 

## 2. Round-trip via canonical EDN — `^cedn`

`^cedn` is the canonical-EDN CLI from the sibling repo
([canonical-edn](https://github.com/franks42/canonical-edn)). Pipe a
Nushell value through it for byte-stable output suitable for hashing
or signing. Different key orders produce identical bytes (and so
identical hashes):

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/table
(let [hash-of (fn [m]
                (-> (nu-> m "from edn | to edn | ^cedn | sha256sum")
                    str/trim
                    (str/split #"\s")
                    first))]
  [{:value "{:a 1, :b 2}" :sha256 (hash-of {:a 1 :b 2})}
   {:value "{:b 2, :a 1}" :sha256 (hash-of {:b 2 :a 1})}])
```

Both rows should show the same digest — `^cedn` normalizes key order and
whitespace before the hash is computed. Same hash a bb program would
produce via `(sha256 (cedn/canonical-bytes v))` directly.

## 3. UUIDv7 generation — `^uuidv7`

`^uuidv7` (from [uuidv7.cljc](https://github.com/franks42/uuidv7.cljc))
emits EDN with `--format edn`. Pipe it through `from edn` to a Nushell
record, drop the noisy 96-bit counter, render as a single-row table:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/table
[(nu->edn nil "^uuidv7 gen --format edn | from edn | reject counter | to edn")]
```

Generate a fresh UUIDv7, parse it via the CLI's `parse` subcommand,
extract the embedded timestamp:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/code
(nu->edn nil
  "^uuidv7 gen
   | str trim
   | ^uuidv7 parse $in
   | from edn
   | get datetime
   | to edn")
```

The whole flow stays inside Nushell, including `$in` substitution and
typed extraction via `get datetime`.

## 4. Three-tool composition

Generate a UUIDv7, parse to a record, attach context, canonicalize,
hash. Three external CLIs (`^uuidv7`, `^cedn`, `sha256sum`), one
Nushell pipe, structured data round-tripping the typed boundary.

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/code
(str/trim
  (nu-> nil
    "^uuidv7 gen --format edn
     | from edn
     | insert source 'demo-notebook'
     | insert at (date now)
     | to edn
     | ^cedn
     | sha256sum"))
```

The result is a deterministic content hash for "this UUIDv7, attributed
to this source, observed at this timestamp." A bb script could compute
the same hash directly via the cedn library — but the Nushell pipe
makes the composition visible in one line of shell.

## 5. Chart from a Nushell-filtered dataset

Push raw data through `nu` for filtering / sorting, hand the result
off to Vega-Lite for plotting:

```{.clojure .bb}
^:kind/vega-lite
{:data {:values
        (nu->edn
          [{:hour "08" :requests 142}
           {:hour "09" :requests 358}
           {:hour "10" :requests 412}
           {:hour "11" :requests 287}
           {:hour "12" :requests 199}
           {:hour "13" :requests 88}
           {:hour "14" :requests 51}]
          "from edn | where requests > 100 | sort-by hour | to edn")}
 :mark "bar"
 :encoding {:x {:field :hour     :type :ordinal      :title "Hour"}
            :y {:field :requests :type :quantitative :title "Requests"}}}
```

## Where this is going

`nu->` / `nu->edn` could mature into a small shared library:

- **stderr capture and propagation** — currently a nu pipeline error
  silently produces empty stdout; a real helper should surface stderr
  alongside the parse error
- **exit-code awareness** — non-zero from any external in the pipe
  should raise, not return nil
- **multi-form streaming variant** — `nu->edn` over `to edn --lines`
  could yield a lazy seq of forms, matching nu's incremental behavior
  on the producer side
- **pipeline-shape pre-validation** — refuse pipelines that don't end
  with `to edn` when called via `nu->edn`
- **`--meta` integration** — auto-attach Quarto block context (file,
  line, run id) as Clojure reader metadata for downstream auditing

The compositional pattern this demos — typed transforms inside Nushell
on the EDN-bytes side, byte-level operations as `^cedn` / `^uuidv7` /
`sha256sum` filters — is the **typed-value boundary principle** that
`nu_plugin_edn` is built around. Quarto + Babqua makes it explorable
inside a reproducible notebook.

## Requirements

- [Nushell](https://www.nushell.sh/book/installation.html) 0.112.2+ on PATH
- [Babashka](https://github.com/babashka/babashka#installation) on PATH
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) on PATH
- [Babqua](https://scicloj.github.io/babqua/) installed in this project (`quarto add scicloj/babqua`)
- [`nu_plugin_edn`](https://github.com/franks42/nu_plugin_edn) registered and `plugin use edn` in `config.nu`
- For sections 2-4: [`^cedn`](https://github.com/franks42/canonical-edn) and [`^uuidv7`](https://github.com/franks42/uuidv7.cljc) on PATH

Render with: `quarto render nu-pipelines.qmd`
